Ingest the unified BMF into entity, name and address

Source: R/md-ingest-bmf.R
md_ingest_bmf.Rd

Reads the pinned BMF parquet and writes its rows into the three core tables. Idempotent: re-running replaces the BMF's own rows rather than accumulating, and leaves every other source's rows alone, so a newer BMF can be loaded into a database that already holds Schedule I, the return headers and the rest.

Usage

md_ingest_bmf(version, con = NULL, validate = TRUE)

md_validate_bmf(con)

Arguments

version

The pinned bmf_unified version, e.g. "v2026-08-11".

con

A connection from md_db(). Opened and closed here if NULL.

validate

Run md_validate() on each table and stop on failure.

Value

A named vector of the BMF's own row counts, invisibly.

What this does and does not populate

The BMF is a snapshot, not a panel (§4), so this fills the identity spine and the current name and address. It writes the resolved-attribute columns as NULL and leaves them for md_ingest_ntee(), which reads the canonical NTEE crosswalk - the only source that can supply the rule and the agreement flag the triple requires. The BMF's own ntee_code_raw is carried through so the recomputation has its input, but the BMF's nteev2 rendering is deliberately not copied: it carries the specialty double-encoding defect (?md_ntee_canonical).

Layer assignment

bmf_active means "in the current active BMF release" (§3a), which in this file is last_vintage_ym equal to the newest vintage present. Everything else is bmf_inactive. status_code is carried separately rather than conflated with layer, because status is mutable and layer is provenance (§4).

Loading into a database that already has other sources

This used to CREATE OR REPLACE all three tables, which deleted every other source's rows and made the BMF loadable only as the first step of a fresh build. It now deletes and re-inserts only its own rows, in one transaction:

  • name and address: rows with source = 'bmf'.

  • entity: rows from any earlier BMF load, plus any row an earlier ingest wrote for an EIN this file contains. The BMF is the identity spine, so its row replaces a filer_only, approved_only or other placeholder for the same EIN.

  • An EIN that an earlier BMF load had but this file does not, and that another source's name, address or entity_event row still refers to, is put back with the layer a fresh build would give it: that of the earliest-built source still naming it (approved_only for 1023-EZ, filer_only for the 990 filings and schedules, postcard_only, revoked_only). No row is left pointing at a missing entity.

Replaced rows lose whatever later steps wrote onto them, and the new BMF rows get new name_id/address_id values. After a re-ingest, re-run the steps that follow the ingests in dev/build-matchdb.R (NTEE, geocode, guards, derived columns with incremental = TRUE, compaction, groups, keys, clusters, statistics). The ingest prints this reminder when it replaced anything.
